solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Accountant tucking into reddish-purple almondy biscuit (8)

indicatorNotes.tucking into: the accountant tucks himself inside the colour word

annotation.surface: An accountant enjoying a purple-tinted biscuit with his tea.
annotation.walkthrough: CA, a chartered accountant, is a standard crossword abbreviation; here it sits after the first two letters of MAROON.
annotation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small biscuit made with ground almonds.

entries.clue: Supplier of oxygen required at first for passenger plane (8)

indicatorNotes.at first: take only the opening letter of 'required'

blocks.note: an air line is the hose feeding a diver oxygen

annotation.surface: A diver or patient insisting an oxygen supply comes first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supplier of oxygen' looks like AIR, but that leaves LINER unexplained; the whole phrase is an air line, the hose that carries breathing air.
annotation.definitionFit: An airliner is a large aircraft carrying passengers.

entries.clue: Loyalty shown by chap caught in hold (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the chap and 'caught' go inside the word for hold

blocks.note: any man's name will do for chap

annotation.surface: A man held prisoner who stays loyal to his captors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold' is the verb, as in holding a view, not a ship's hold or a grip; C for caught comes from cricket scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: Allegiance is loyalty owed to a ruler or cause.

entries.clue: Exotic blooming country is hot (10)

blocks.note: flowers that are blooming are out

annotation.surface: A travel brochure: a strange land full of flowers and heat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' can be read as a mild British swear word, but here it means in flower.
annotation.definitionFit: Outlandish means strange and foreign-seeming, as exotic does.

entries.clue: At sea warn prince, finding toothed marine mammal (7)

indicatorNotes.At sea: all at sea = confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

annotation.surface: A sailor warning a prince that something with teeth is in the water.
annotation.walkthrough: Hal is the go-to crossword prince, from Shakespeare's Henry IV plays.
annotation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale whose male grows a long spiral tusk, a tooth.

entries.clue: Confuse hanger-on holding line (4)

indicatorNotes.holding: the hanger-on holds the line inside it

blocks.note: a bur(r) is a seed head that clings to clothing

annotation.surface: A clingy follower holding a line, muddling things.
annotation.walkthrough: A hanger-on is usually a person; here it is the prickly bur that sticks to you.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean to make something unclear or muddled.

entries.clue: Crossing Welsh river, came across old firearm (6)

indicatorNotes.Crossing: the verb straddles the river, so it goes round it

blocks.note: the Usk flows through south Wales

annotation.surface: A walker fording a Welsh river finds an antique gun on the bank.
annotation.walkthrough: The Usk is a river in south Wales, a crossword regular among short river names.
annotation.definitionFit: A musket is a long smoothbore gun of the pre-rifle era.

entries.clue: Barefaced attorney finally upholding women’s contract (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of attorney
indicatorNotes.upholding: in a down clue, the first part sits beneath the women's W, holding it up

blocks.note: barefaced and arrant both mean shameless, out-and-out

annotation.surface: A brazen lawyer backing a women's agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upholding' works only because this is a down entry: ARRANTY stands below W and supports it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a guarantee to repair or replace goods is a binding agreement with the buyer.

entries.clue: University invested in Lamb’s complete works? Praise the Lord! (8)

indicatorNotes.invested in: the university is put inside, as money is invested in a fund

blocks.note: ALL (complete) ELIA: Charles Lamb wrote his essays as Elia

annotation.surface: A university buying a set of Lamb's writings, to a cry of joy.
annotation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb, the 19th-century English essayist, published the Essays of Elia under that pen name, so all of Lamb's works are ALL ELIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Alleluia is the Hebrew-derived cry meaning praise the Lord.

entries.clue: Danish prince losing head about king’s band (6)

indicatorNotes.losing head: drop the first letter of Hamlet
indicatorNotes.about: what is left goes round the king

annotation.surface: Hamlet beheaded, which might make one think of the king's crime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' could be a group of players in Elsinore, but it is the thing worn round an arm.
annotation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band worn round the upper arm.

entries.clue: Crook in US city with last of beer in mug (10)

indicatorNotes.last of: take the final letter of beer
indicatorNotes.in mug: that R goes inside the word for mug

blocks.note: a beaker is a mug-like cup

annotation.surface: A villain in an American city with the dregs of his beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mug' suggests a dupe, which fits the crime story, but it is a drinking vessel here.
annotation.definitionFit: A crook is a criminal, one who breaks the law.

entries.clue: One in opposition essential to Victorian times (4)

indicatorNotes.essential to: the answer lies in the essence, the inside, of the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: A contrarian who was a fixture of the Victorian age.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essential to' means contained in: the four letters span the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who opposes something.

entries.clue: Reform apt in a lone Italian citizen (10)

annotation.surface: Political reform proposed by a single Italian.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but its letters are needed in the fodder; only 'Reform' is left over as the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A native of Naples, the southern Italian city, whose Greek name was Neapolis.

entries.clue: In Congo, age dreadfully, like some greyhounds? (5-5)

indicatorNotes.dreadfully: the letters are treated badly, rearranged

annotation.surface: Racing dogs in the Congo getting old badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is fodder, not a link. The question mark flags the definition: an ocean greyhound was a fast transatlantic liner.
annotation.definitionFit: Some greyhounds are ships, the fast liners called greyhounds of the sea, and they are ocean-going.

entries.clue: Enliven Spanish port cutting current charge (10)

indicatorNotes.cutting: the port cuts in between the two other words

blocks.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, north-west Spain

annotation.surface: A Spanish port livened up by cutting its electricity bill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current charge' reads as an electricity bill; the two words work separately, the first in its sense of fashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: To invigorate is to fill with life and energy.

entries.clue: Frenzied French worker perhaps in charge (7)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: an ant is one example of a worker

annotation.surface: A harassed French employee who has been left in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worker' in crosswords is very often ANT or BEE.
annotation.definitionFit: Frantic and frenzied both mean wildly agitated.

entries.clue: Half-heartedly excite popular old Asian islander (8)

indicatorNotes.Half-heartedly: half of the heart of FILLIP, the double L, is removed

blocks.note: FILLIP (to excite, stimulate) losing one of its central Ls

annotation.surface: Someone giving a lukewarm welcome to a once-popular visitor from Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: A fillip is a stimulus, and as a verb it means to excite. Its heart is LL, and losing half of that leaves FILIP.
annotation.definitionFit: A Filipino is a native of the Philippines, an Asian island nation.

entries.clue: Acolyte unknown where food is dished out (7)

blocks.note: a server assists the priest at the altar
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

annotation.surface: An anonymous altar boy serving at a soup kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Server' is itself a food word, which helps the surface; here it is the church sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A servery is a counter or room from which meals are served.

entries.clue: Responsive to stimulus concerning voice (8)

annotation.surface: A singer whose voice responds to any prompt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Voice' means a grammatical voice, active or passive, not a singing voice.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something that reacts is responding to what acts on it.

entries.clue: Aimed to resolve despair (7)

indicatorNotes.resolve: the letters are broken up and settled in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone who set out to beat their hopelessness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' reads as determination, which suits the surface; as an indicator it means to break down into parts.
annotation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim at a goal.

entries.clue: Boss dropping a pipe by new Bavarian wear (10)

indicatorNotes.dropping: the A falls out of the word for boss

blocks.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

annotation.surface: A boss putting down his pipe next to some new clothes from Bavaria.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' suggests tobacco, fitting a Bavarian scene, but it is a garden hose.
annotation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are the leather shorts traditionally worn in Bavaria.

entries.clue: Teacher digesting trashy paper, a formidable type (6)

indicatorNotes.digesting: the teacher takes the paper inside

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher
a rag is a low-quality newspaper

annotation.surface: A fearsome teacher reading a tabloid.
annotation.walkthrough: A don is an Oxford or Cambridge academic, and a rag a trashy newspaper.
annotation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fierce, intimidating person, often a stern older woman.

entries.clue: Sticky substance lying around a Pacific island (4)

indicatorNotes.lying around: the sticky stuff surrounds the A

annotation.surface: Litter of chewing gum on a tropical island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying around' reads as litter, but it means placed round the A.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by type: an island in Micronesia, governed as a US territory.

entries.clue: Very quiet in middle of supper? (10)

blocks.note: the surface reads this as a hush falling over the meal
the setter's reading: the two letters at the centre of the word supper, taken as a musical marking

annotation.surface: A hushed dinner party, conversation dying away mid-meal.
annotation.walkthrough: Music scores mark very quiet passages pp, short for pianissimo, and pp is exactly what sits in the middle of supper.
annotation.definitionFit: Pianissimo is the musical direction for very soft playing.

entries.clue: Cricketer’s blunder (4)

blocks.note: a fielding position close behind the batter, and the fielder standing there

annotation.surface: A cricketer dropping a catch.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, the slips are fielders standing close behind the batter, beside the wicketkeeper, and each player there is called a slip.
annotation.definitionFit: Slip names both the fielder and a small error.

entries.clue: One practised a form of civil disobedience in compound (6)

blocks.clueFragment: practised a form of civil disobedience
blocks.note: sat in, as protesters do in a sit-in

annotation.surface: A protester who staged a sit-in on a fenced site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like a walled enclosure for the protest, but it is a chemical.
annotation.definitionFit: Isatin is an orange-red chemical compound, used in making dyes.

entries.clue: Midday issue with denial for one retracted (8)

indicatorNotes.for: 'for' as in 'swap A for B': one thing stands in place of another, so NO takes the place of an I
indicatorNotes.retracted: drawn back, so the result reads backwards

blocks.note: an edition is an issue of a publication
i = one, and it is the second I of EDITION that is swapped out

annotation.surface: A lunchtime announcement retracting an earlier denial.
annotation.walkthrough: Swapping the second I of EDITION for NO gives EDITNOON, which read backwards is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: tide in its old sense of time, as in Yuletide, so the time of noon.

entries.clue: Name of bank used by the Spanish? Nonsense (8)

blocks.note: Dogger Bank, a sandbank in the North Sea

annotation.surface: A British bank's name being mangled by Spanish speakers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but Dogger Bank is a sandbank in the North Sea, familiar from the BBC shipping forecast.
annotation.definitionFit: Doggerel is trivial, badly made verse, near enough nonsense.
